classification.method: expected class from the harness (new $LATEST config -> cold; new published version -> restore; reused environment -> warm), checked against REPORT (Init Duration / Restore Duration / neither)

conclusion: Resetting only the cache metadata between requests changes the first request after a SnapStart restore by -0.293 s on 0xd40. On CPU part 0xd40 (as read from /proc/cpuinfo; n=[54, 51]) the restored first request's REPORT Duration falls from 0.687 to 0.394 s (-42.6%, delta -0.293 s, 95% CI [-0.301, -0.282]); on 0xd0c (n=[6, 9]) from 1.064 to 0.678 s (-36.3%). In every (round, CPU part) cell every e12 row is faster than every dor row. Restore first request total (Restore Duration + Duration) on 0xd40: 3.956 -> 3.651 s (-7.7%, CI [-0.345, -0.240]). Lambda's own Restore Duration, which runs before any function code, is unchanged (+0.005 s, CI [-0.046, +0.032]), as it should be. The hypothesis (about 0.3 s, half of 0.68 s) holds. Warm: on 0xd40 steady-state inference p50 0.467 -> 0.460 s (-1.56%, CI [-0.033, +0.011]); paired by request and round the median ratio is 0.9844 (CI [0.969387, 1.002377], 54 cells), so the hypothesised ~2% warm gain is not established. The warm effect splits by request: requests no longer than one the environment already ran change by -4.6% (0xd40, median over requests), and requests that reach further into the caches than any earlier one in their environment change by +1.6%. The likely reason is that e12 defers the first touch of never-written cache pages from the clear into that request's forward; this is an inference (Lambda allows no fault counting) and the split is confounded with the fixed warm request order. Cold: the first request total is unchanged (-0.103 s, CI [-0.175, +0.002]); the 25 s S3 download still binds. Correctness: 0 errors (no client:ReadTimeoutError) and 0 class mismatches in 1320 invocations; 840 of 840 answers P1's reference covers are bit-identical to it, and 660 of 660 e12 answers equal the dor answers for the same request and CPU part (P1's five requests plus four stress requests: a 16-question fork over a 2.8k-token state, then short requests on the cells it left). Offline on arm64 (not Lambda): P1's own shim, the dormant switch and DEC_CLEAR_DATA=0 return identical answers and identical hidden-state bytes for every request in 6 shuffled orders x 3 repeats (972 rows, pass=True), with no dependence on what ran before. The shim reported its mode from inside every environment (dor 1, e12 0). Max memory used moves by +2.5 MB cold and +0.0 MB restored (p50, 0xd40). Scope: this applies to Lambda (SnapStart) only, not to SageMaker-hosted models (operator scope note, 2026-10-21). The saving is the first touch of SnapStart-restored cache memory, and the warm effect alone is not established; SageMaker was not measured here. Recommendation: adopt DEC_CLEAR_DATA=0 for Lambda SnapStart deployments; a ladder rung should re-measure it with E10 (smaller n_ctx shrinks the same buffers) and consider touching the caches once before the snapshot to remove the deferred first-touch cost on long requests.

host.note: Read inside the function on each environment's first invocation, after P1's handler returned: /proc/cpuinfo, /proc/self/auxv, os.sched_getaffinity, /sys/fs/cgroup. 'unknown' = not exposed. CPU part and features are reported as read; no Graviton generation is inferred.

e12.status_rule: headline CIs from CPU parts with at least 3 samples per arm

warm_by_reach.method: for every environment (env_id) in invocation order, a warm row is new_max if its input_tokens exceed every earlier row's in that environment (cold or restore probe included), else within_seen; ratio = median(e12) / median(dor) per request; _median_ratio = median over requests
warm_by_reach.note: descriptive: the warm passes run in a fixed request order, so reach and request size are confounded; the order is not shuffled on Lambda (the offline check shuffles it for correctness)

warm_paired.method: one cell per (round, request, CPU part) with both arms; ratio = median(e12) / median(dor) of engine latency_ms; median over cells; ci95 = bootstrap over cells (4,000, seed 12)

assessment.fixed_host: not used: the change removes memory writes (and, by inference, page faults) on SnapStart-restored memory, which a fixed EC2 host cannot reproduce; the offline arm64 check is used for correctness only

headline_total.note: Restore Duration is Lambda's snapshot restore, before function code runs, and E12 does not change it; its within-cell range is several times the Duration effect, so some total cells fall inside the control range although every total cell is negative

assessment.rerun: not needed: in every (round, CPU part) cell the targeted phase's delta is negative and at least 90% of row pairs have e12 faster, and every cell of the total is negative

target_phase.note: the range rule fails in cells where one dor row is slow (e.g. one 3.4 s Duration); every cell's delta is negative and its p_e12_below_dor is at least the floor

host_variability.method: Within each round, both arms' restore waves start at the same moment, so the arms share the round and the minute. Cells are (round, CPU part as read from /proc/cpuinfo per invocation); a cell's outcome compares the e12-minus-dor median delta with the dor observations' range in that cell, and p_e12_below_dor is the share of (e12 row, dor row) pairs in the cell where e12 is faster. Rows without a CPU identity are counted, never treated as a stratum. No Graviton generation is inferred.
host_variability.metrics: restore report_duration (the first request after a restore, the phase E12 targets); restore first_request_total (Restore Duration + Duration); restore Restore Duration (not targeted: a control); cold first_request_inference

hypothesis: Half of the first forward after a SnapStart restore (0.68 s against 0.24 s warm, P3) is memset inside llama_kv_cache::clear and llama_memory_recurrent::clear: the per-request llama_memory_clear(mem, true) zeroes every K/V and recurrent buffer, and after a restore that is the first touch of those pages. At llama.cpp f74e2fa6a the zeroing is not needed for correct results: the KQ mask gives every empty attention cell -INFINITY, and the recurrent cache zeroes one state row in the graph (build_rs, rs_z) and copies it into every cell a sequence starts in. Resetting only the cache metadata (llama_memory_clear(mem, false)) should make the restored first request about 0.3 s faster and warm requests about 2% faster, with bit-identical answers.
